terms.grammar: ōvum, ōvī n., with Paschālis, Paschāle; plural ōva Paschālia
terms.comment: A description of ours: we have found no term for an Easter egg in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. It joins the classical ōvum to Paschālis, the Christian Latin adjective for Easter, as Traupman builds arbor nātālīcia for the Christmas tree. For dyed red eggs, ōva rubra.

phrases.english: We dye the Easter eggs red.

phrases.latin: Ōva inter sē collīdāmus: utrum frangētur?
phrases.english: Let’s knock our eggs together: which one will break?

sources: Lewis & Short: ovum · Lewis & Short: paschalis · Lewis & Short: collido
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Christian: Easter.
